articles.title: Cooking with Tom Kerridge, the Michelin ‘meatfluencer’
articles.summary: The star chef demystified the restaurant scene with his love of a welcoming pub. Now he explains why hospitality is in crisis – and how to make a sublime venison chilli.
body: Tom Kerridge is the king of meat: first as a chef, transforming pub classics like pork belly into Michelin-starred fare at The Hand and Flowers in Marlow 20 years ago, and later opening The Butcher’s Tap and Grill in the same village; then as a cookery writer: his Outdoor Cooking – The Ultimate Modern Barbecue Bible of 2021 is well named, being both as comprehensive and as worshipful as a holy book; and recently as a “meat-fluencer”, making gorgeous skills videos on Instagram and YouTube.

That was just destiny, he says (more or less). “When you’re cooking in a classic brigade system, the sections are like a larder: you’ve got starters, you’ve got garnish, you’ve got meat and fish, you’ve got pastry. The meat is the lead section, where the most experienced chef is, because that’s where you land when you’ve learned to treat vegetables with love and respect. If you fuck up cabbage, it doesn’t cost a lot.” It’s true, it doesn’t, but if you saw the care Kerridge puts into dicing an onion – peeling its layers apart like he’s making a mosaic, assiduous even about half an inch of waste – of an onion – you’d know that love and respect aren’t really about money.

articles.title: Tim Dowling: I’ve been replaced by a younger model … it’s a relief
articles.summary: My wife has summarily dismissed me from outdoor duties, in favour of ‘Gardening Steve’. Inevitably, there’s a catch. My wife wants to hire someone to put the garden in order. She knows I’ll object, because it’s really something I should be doing, but she also knows I won’t do it.
body: As part of her campaign my wife has let it be known that paying someone to fix the garden is no reflection on me, because I’m a businessman with little time to devote to things of the soil.
“If you’re promising this will never be held against me at any point in the future,” I say.
“And with all your free time, you can finally do the kitchen table,” she says. I think: oh no.

We bought our kitchen table 30 years ago from a workshop that was throwing it away. It’s made of four old roof rafters knocked together, and the top needs sanding down and refinishing about every five years. I do it, on average, once every 10.

articles.title: Behind Edward Buchanan’s Hub for Black Creatives
articles.summary: The industry legend has opened a new center to house and foster under-represented talent. And he’s done it without a hint of outside investment.
body: For Ohio-born designer Edward Buchanan, Black industry mentors changed his life. While finishing his studies at New York’s Parsons School of Design, designer Gordon Henderson put him forward for interviews at major fashion houses, while Rodney Patterson gave him a tip off about an opening at Bottega Veneta, where he would become the first ready-to-wear design director. Now, more than three decades on, the creative director and knitwear specialist has opened a self-funded foundation to continue that lineage.

The result is a 400-square-meter building located in NoLo — a historically working-class and multicultural district of Milan — dedicated to fostering and guiding creative talents from under-represented communities, including people of color (POC), queer, and female cultural practitioners. Crucially, Buchanan will ensure the non-profit remains financially autonomous, with no outside investment. He’s calling it The Situation, after the design consultancy he co-founded in 2012.

articles.title: The Most Beautiful Mountains in the World—for Climbing to the Top or Admiring From Afar
articles.summary: From Ecuador's snowcapped Cotopaxi to Malaysia's lush Kinabalu, the most beautiful mountains in the world offer dramatic landscapes, biodiverse climates, and something for every kind of curious visitor.
body: Though you may not be able to climb all of the most beautiful mountains in the world, you certainly can admire their grandeur from a distance. Rugged and immovable yet inspiring, often with vastly different climates across their bases and peaks, these sloping landforms are as alluring for scaling as they are for scenic views.

Whether you're looking for rare flora and fauna at a mountain's lush foothills in Borneo, fields of wildflower with distant slopes in Washington state, or jagged spires of granite in Argentina, these landmarks and their pristine surroundings are ideal for outdoor activities such as horseback riding, hiking, cycling, camping, or even strolling. Below, explore the 10 most stunning mountains across the globe, which all offer something distinct for every type of traveler.

articles.title: The Best Korean Skin-Care Products People Actually Buy
articles.summary: Achieve glass skin with the best Korean skincare products according to K-Beauty experts. Shop top brands like Laneige, Beauty of Joseon & CosRx.
body: While many of the best Korean skincare products are available in the U.S. thanks to the likes of Amazon and Soko Glam, I still couldn’t wait to touch down in store to try some things I’d been eyeing myself. Perhaps because I’m a beauty editor, I’m not one to wander around a beauty store; but my local Olive Young had my full attention. On three separate occasions, I spent upwards of an hour going shelf by shelf to study what products Koreans actually reach for.

As you’ve likely noticed, K-beauty has steadily grown from a niche category to the global mainstream over the last few years, thanks in large part to the power of social media. “While Amazon and TikTok are leading the K-beauty sales, the category is sure to see major growth this year as American consumers discover new products via social media, Korean culture (think: K-Pop and K-Drama), and in-store launches,” Sarah Chung Park, founder and CEO of Landing International, tells Vogue.

articles.title: Steal My Food Itinerary: 3 Days in Sifnos, Greece
articles.summary: It felt like everyone I know traveled to Greece this summer. Friends chose Zakynthos, Crete, Naxos, Ikaria. I opted for Sifnos, one of the Cyclades’ most celebrated food destinations but still, thankfully, relatively under the radar internationally.
body: Just 3 hours from Athens by ferry, this Cycladic island is best experienced around the table.

Our trip landed in the middle of August — peak tourist season in the Mediterranean — but it never felt cramped. And now that summer has come to a close, what crowds there were have thinned and temperatures are more forgiving, yet peak-season produce is still finding its way into dishes across the island. So now is an even better time to experience Sifnos.

Getting there means starting in Athens, where ferries come in and out of the port of Piraeus from all across the Aegean and Ionian seas. The 2.5 to 3-hour trip from Athens to Sifnos is a thrill — worthy of a few Dramamine tablets if you’re prone to seasickness — with incredible views of the islands you pass along the way. The Aegean really is a different shade of blue; it’s tempting to gaze into it from the deck the whole way.

articles.title: Boston Is One of America’s Best Sushi Cities—Here’s Where to Make a Reservation
articles.summary: From lavish omakase counters with Hermès plates and a Michelin-star winner to unfussy, neighborhood gems, here are the Boston spots that our sushi snobs (yes, there are many here) rely on.
body: If there’s anything I know about Boston, it’s that this is a city that knows its seafood. Because of location and fishing heritage, we sling lobster rolls and oysters and fried clams by the bucket—so it should come as no surprise that sushi, too, has become a serious part of the city’s more upscale dining culture. Yes, travelers come here to experience our classic sea coast and clam shacks, but increasingly you’ll find that Boston has a robust enough sushi scene to excite international visitors, too—one that benefits not only from our abundant local fisheries, but also the international demand that make it possible to source special ingredients like fish flown in straight from Japan.

articles.summary: From cool everyday looks to statement ensembles, recreate the season’s top fashion week outfits, inspired by the street style scene at Milan Fashion Week.
body: All products featured on Vogue are independently selected by our editors. However, we may earn affiliate revenue on this article and commission when you buy something.

Ciao Milano! Following the Vogue World: Milan kickoff, MFW is in full swing, with industry insiders crowding the city’s historic cobblestone streets in looks that embody the Italian city’s love of femininity with hints of relaxed tailoring. Vogue Italia fashion market editor Marta Oldrini was among them, showing up outside Prada’s spring 2027 debut in her signature uniform of layers on layers with an It accessory in the mix. Others sported everything from statement skirts and leopard-print outerwear to flashes of r oyal purple —and pale pink. The fashion verdict? Fall outfit inspiration is taking a front-row seat.

We spotted Dries Van Noten skants with sumptuous suede handbags, flannel shirts tied loosely at the waist with simple long-sleeve white tees, and a slew of statement accessories that take everyday ensembles to new heights.
The month-long fashion extravaganza’s European tour has no plans of stopping. Next up? Paris, baby! Until then, shop ten Milan Fashion Week trends to inspire your next great look.
